summary: This humorous feature surveys a series of photography and digital art festivals running from September to December 2024, showing how the art world is embracing virtual reality, holograms, glitch art, memes and kinetic digital imagery. It also highlights the 'Aperture Apostles', who defend analog film photography. The piece concludes that images will keep evolving whether made with film or binary.
one_line: A playful overview of fall 2024 photography and digital art festivals, from VR and holograms to glitch art, memes, kinetic art and analog film.
key_facts: The 'Virtuality Coup' is a virtual reality art event beginning September 12th at the Expanse Gallery, curated by Lysander Q. Pixel.
The Hologram Happening is slated for September 28th and is orchestrated by illusionist Iris Lente, placing holograms on downtown streets and squares.
Passersby photograph Iris Lente's holograms and post captions like 'Spotted: Ghosts of Pixels Past.'
Everette 'Error' Smith holds the Glitch Gala on October 3rd, presenting digital glitches as the highest form of impromptu art.
The Film Forever Festival is scheduled for October 10th, hosted by the analog photographers calling themselves the 'Aperture Apostles' and curated by Diana Silvera.
Diana Silvera and her group argue for the tangible medium of film, the authenticity of grain and the ceremony of shot staging.
The Meme Monarchy debuts November 1st under curator Taylor 'Troll' Davies and treats viral memes as fine art.
Taylor 'Troll' Davies argues 'Art evolves,' and the show may place Pepe the Frog next to abstract expressionist work.
Art in Motion takes place December 1st, featuring kinetic digital representations moving across walls, floors and ceilings.
Art in Motion is conceived by multimedia artist Kinetica, real name Keith O. Botic, whose work can leave patrons dizzily amazed or mildly nauseous.
The article is dated to the start of September 2024 and frames these festivals as moving beyond conventional easels and gallery walls.
